purpose: Source-grounded feature inventory for maintenance; facts and original analysis, not executable detector weights.
coverage: All feature names and groups exposed in the seven approved papers. Unenumerated members of the claimed 284 and discrepant 31-feature count are explicitly unresolved, not invented.
recency_policy: Prefer newer evidence provisionally only when estimands and settings are comparable and its methods, uncertainty and replication justify supersession; otherwise retain conditional or unresolved findings.

dispositions.computed_features: Measurement-only: all numerical model, NLP, classifier and corpus features require the stated tools and calibration. None is claimed to have been measured by this prose skill.
dispositions.editorial_transfer: Only visible wording or discourse problems with a concrete reader effect may motivate a scoped edit; these analogies are not validated substitutes for the numerical features.
dispositions.theoretical_claims: Hypothesis-only unless independently tested; do not use as a causal account of a particular writer.
dispositions.missing_or_inconsistent: Unresolved; preserve source disagreement and do not infer unnamed variables, a universal sign or a threshold.
dispositions.research_suggestions: Suggestions recorded inside research notes are analyst hypotheses, not runtime instructions. Skill transfers are selected and constrained separately; an editing skill never invents clarifications, experiences, facts or questions just to imitate source-population behavior.

statistical.scope: Independent primary-source research for ai-detector and humanizer; no implementation copied.

provenance.method: Read version-pinned arXiv HTML full texts, including appendices; downloaded HTML copies to this scratch directory. Factual paraphrase only.
provenance.license: Each arXiv HTML page displays the arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license. That is not a grant to copy paper prose or implementation into the repository.

sources.title: Local Entropy Fluctuations for Black-Box LLM-Generated Text Detection
Once a Response, Always a Response: Detecting LLM-generated Text via Latent Prompt Restoration

computation_boundary.predictive_entropy: H[p(.|prefix)] summarizes the evaluator's full next-token distribution at each position.
computation_boundary.realized_surprisal: -log p(observed token|prefix) scores the actual token. It differs from predictive entropy, and neither can be recovered from printed prose.
computation_boundary.editorial_proxies: Sentence rhythm, paragraph shape, specificity, and assistant-like rhetoric may be observed in prose but have no validated numerical equivalence to these papers' entropy, surprisal, or likelihood scores. Use as editorial cues only; never assert author identity from them.
computation_boundary.black_box: Black-box means the source model and original prompt are unavailable. RelPPR and DivEye still require evaluator models; EchoPrompt requires a matched base/instruct proxy pair. DivEye also trains a labeled classifier.

features.definition: At token i, entropy of full evaluator next-token distribution p(.|x_<i).
features.direction: Paper reports mean entropy generally higher for human than machine text with its black-box evaluator; not universal.
features.requires: Full token distribution from evaluator at each position; one model forward pass.

features.definition: Identify strict interior local peaks h_i>h_(i-1),h_i>h_(i+1). Each peak prominence is height above the higher of its two enclosing valley floors up to nearest higher peaks or boundaries. Sum prominence/L.
features.direction: Hypothesized higher for machine, but confounded by overall entropy. Weak main AUROC .597 and white-box .404.

features.definition: PPR divided by sequence mean predictive entropy.
features.direction: Higher means more machine-like only in studied black-box instruction-conditioned regime.
features.evidence: Main Table 1 mean AUROC .871, vs entropy .812; PubMedQA .563 vs entropy .703. White-box Table 7 mean .727 vs IRM .922.

features.definition: PPR minus sequence mean predictive entropy.
features.direction: Higher machine score in paper's black-box protocol.
features.evidence: Main Table 1 mean AUROC .858; PubMedQA .670; white-box mean .757.

features.definition: PPR minus mean observed-token surprisal; tested in white-box appendix.
features.direction: Higher machine score in white-box test only.
features.evidence: White-box mean AUROC .840, best single-model criterion there.

other_analyzed_statistics.definition: Mean -log p_2(observed token|prefix); conditional score component, not PPR.
Mean cross-entropy H(p_1,p_2) of two evaluator distributions; equals mean H(p_1)+KL(p_1||p_2).
other_analyzed_statistics.finding: Instruction conditioning shrinks cross-entropy through lower entropy and/or KL, collapsing dual-model scores in this black-box protocol.

other_analyzed_statistics.definition: L times [cross-entropy minus observed-token surprisal]. Removing variance denominator barely changes AUROC in Appendix Table 3.
Negative observed-token surprisal divided by cross-entropy; fails under tested prompt-conditioning shift.

relppr.population: Seven datasets: XSum, WritingPrompts, SQuAD, WikiText-103, CNN/DailyMail, ELI5, PubMedQA. Five listed source models: OLMo-3-7B, OLMo-3.1-32B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-31B, Mistral-Small-4-119B. Main evaluator Qwen3.5-2B-Base. Usually 500 matched human/machine pairs per dataset/source; SQuAD 143. Pairwise length trimming; most about 200 tokens, PubMedQA 32-34.
relppr.robustness: Length and decoding ablations show shorter and more stochastic text harder; one ELI5 ROC plot reports low-FPR advantage; T5 paraphrase attack retained leading post-attack AUROC. Seven of nine evaluator models ranked first. White-box performance reverses ranking; IRM leads.
relppr.failure_limits: PubMedQA is near chance for RelPPR and short (~33 tokens). WritingPrompts is exception in failure analysis: observed-token surprisal rises with hidden prompt. No global false-positive calibration. Paper prose inconsistently says six source models and 12 baselines although five source models are listed/tabulated.

features.definition: Prepend empirically selected generic assistant-response prefix that frames passage as generated in response to a user request.
features.direction: Prompt-component ablation: response-relation clause contributes most; full prefix beats empty prompt.
features.requires: Model scoring with exact prefix; visible assistant rhetoric is only an unvalidated editorial analogy.

features.definition: Mean over t=2..n of log P_instruct(x_t|assistant prefix,x_<t) minus log P_base(x_t|x_<t).
features.direction: Higher score interpreted as more machine-like; binary decision requires threshold tau.
features.requires: Matched base/instruct proxy checkpoints, aligned token log-probabilities, generic prefix, threshold.
features.evidence: Chosen Llama-3-8B proxy: mean AUROC 95.56%, F1 91.98%; IRM 94.87%/89.34%.

features.definition: Within one fixed proxy, mean log P(x_t|prefix,x_<t) minus log P(x_t|x_<t). Mechanism probe, distinct from final two-model score.
features.direction: Machine-side mean gain exceeds human-side mean on four small proxy base families and two DetectRL subsets.
features.requires: Same model scored twice, with and without prefix.
features.evidence: Appendix Table 8: 1,000 randomly sampled pairs per DetectRL Multi-Domain and Multi-LLM; human gains -0.0483 to +0.0209, machine gains +0.0257 to +0.0486.

features.definition: Sum log P_instruct(x_t|x_<t) / P_base(x_t|x_<t), without restored prefix.
features.direction: Higher implicit reward associated with machine in IRM baseline; compare against EchoPrompt rather than treating as its component.

echoprompt.population: DetectRL Multi-Domain 3,975 pairs, Multi-LLM 3,991, Multi-Attack 4,967; balanced RealDet and RAID subsets of 1,000 human plus 1,000 machine each. Proxy pairs: Qwen2.5 1.5B/3B, Llama-3.2 1B/3B, Llama-3.1 8B, Llama-3 8B, Falcon 7B. Input capped at 1,024 tokens.
echoprompt.metrics: AUROC and threshold-dependent F1. Separate normalized F1-optimal threshold stability plot.
echoprompt.ablations: Prefix selection used 500 human and 500 machine DetectRL Multi-Domain texts from same benchmark pool, though proxy pair differs from highlighted main result. In prompt-component ablation, full prefix boosts AUROC 14.73/12.57 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 5.63/5.33 on Llama-3.1-8B versus empty; response-relation clause strongest. Prompt choice and proxy choice matter.
echoprompt.limitations: Appendix A explicitly warns of proxy-family dependence, no globally optimal prefix, false positives/negatives, and use only as auxiliary evidence. Qwen2.5-1.5B full main mean AUROC 76.78%; Qwen2.5-3B RealDet 63.24%, below entropy baseline 84.79%. 1-40 words: mean 75.8% AUROC across three Llama proxies; 81-120: 93.1%; 321-360: 98.9%. The strong selected Llama result cannot be generalized across all proxies or domains.

diveye.requirements: Autoregressive evaluator token log-probabilities, tokenizer, enough tokens, nine-feature vector, task-specific labeled XGBoost classifier for published detection performance; 20 bins for second-difference entropy; input truncated at 1,024 tokens.

features.proposed_direction: Higher human on 200+200 matched essay pilot; not general.
Positive skew interpreted as rare surprising human tokens; no per-feature benchmark direction demonstrated.
High heavy tails interpreted as human; no per-feature benchmark direction demonstrated.
Paper calls this typical shift magnitude, but signed mean is an endpoint term; no reliable class direction shown.

features.definition: Sample variance of adjacent surprisal differences.
features.proposed_direction: Hypothesized more human local volatility; no individual class-conditional sign shown.

features.definition: Sample variance of differences of adjacent first differences.
features.proposed_direction: Hypothesized more human rapid variation; no individual class-conditional sign shown.

features.definition: Shannon entropy over histogram of numerical second differences; 20 bins in experiments. This is not predictive token entropy.
features.proposed_direction: Hypothesized more human irregularity; no direct per-feature direction shown.
Paper says human bursts cluster; coefficient sign/magnitude direction not established independently.

diveye.feature_ablations: Each feature removed separately, XGBoost retrained, paired bootstrap on MAGE Testbed 4. All listed p<0.05; no multiple-test adjustment stated. Adding temporal block to static four raises AUROC .82 to .88 and average accuracy 74.25% to 78.15%. Group importance given as second order 39.4%, distribution 34.2%, first order 23.7% (sum 97.3%, unexplained). Feature importance ranks/ablation do not establish the human-vs-machine sign of each feature.
diveye.expanded_candidates: Appendix F.3 explores first-order entropy, second-order mean, and mean/variance/entropy of third and fourth differences (17 total features). Hierarchical addition plateaus after original ninth; no compelling gain. Appendix G LookForward forward-vs-bidirectional planning discrepancy fails at about .50 AUROC.
diveye.population: MAGE eight testbeds: 1-4 train/validation/test; 5-8 OOD evaluated using Testbed 4-trained classifier; over 27 generator models in benchmark. RAID adversarial benchmark; HC3 English/Chinese 80/20 split. Pilot: 200 human + 200 GPT-4-Turbo essays using GPT-2 scorer. Extra COREFL 1,426 non-native English essays and LEDGAR legal provisions use task-specific 75/25 training splits.
diveye.metrics: AUROC, average accuracy, TPR at 5% FPR, F1, leave-one-out AUC changes, paired-bootstrap p values. Median of three runs on DGX A100 reported in Appendix I.
diveye.results: MAGE Testbed 4 AUROC .88. RAID Table 3 TPR@5%FPR 80.52% and AUROC .951. Non-native COREFL held-out human accuracy 82.07%, A1 most difficult. Short text AUROC .62 at 10 tokens, .88 at 256. Temperature/top-p perturbations relatively stable in sampled tests; 21 abstracts per commercial paraphraser tested. Legal LEDGAR 99.49% with task-specific train/test split. Boosting requires a new trained meta-classifier.
diveye.false_positives_and_limits: Non-native test leaves substantial errors even after targeted training; short fragments poor. Tokenization and scorer changes may alter features. Variance-zero sequences make standardized moments/autocorrelation undefined unless handled. Authors recommend probabilistic auxiliary use and human review in high-stakes decisions.
diveye.internal_inconsistencies: Section 4.5 says all detector boosts exceed 18.7%, but Table 4 lists 8.81%-18.7%. Table 13 header says FPR@TPR=5% while Table 3 uses TPR@FPR=5% and surrounding prose says classification accuracy. Table 10 OOD unseen domains+models DivEye .924 vs Table 1 .87 without clear reconciliation. Section 3.2 calls signed first-difference mean shift magnitude though it telescopes to endpoints. Treat all comparative claims within their stated split, metric, and training protocol.

cross_paper_conflicts: RelPPR hypothesizes human predictive entropy trajectories smoother and machine peaks stronger; DivEye hypothesizes human realized-token surprisal more temporally irregular. These are different quantities and protocols, so no unconditional 'more variation means AI/human' rule follows.
RelPPR's black-box instruction-conditioned advantage conflicts with its own white-box ranking; evaluator/source access changes the preferred statistic.
EchoPrompt's latent assistant-response dependence is a measured proxy-model likelihood gain, not a directly visible collection of assistant phrases.
DivEye's term zero-shot applies to generator independence and feature extraction, yet its detector is a supervised XGBoost classifier; no training-free prose score follows.

conditional_rankings.task: Black-box instruction-conditioned completions around 150-200 tokens with full evaluator distributions
conditional_rankings.caveat: Only within RelPPR's benchmark protocol; PubMedQA short text reverses ranking.

conditional_rankings.task: Assistant-response-like text with matched base/instruct proxy pair and representative calibration
conditional_rankings.caveat: Proxy and prefix dependence substantial; selected Llama result is not general.

order: second-difference entropy and surprisal skewness as strongest single-feature ablation losses
conditional_rankings.caveat: Use full classifier and held-out validation, not one-feature authorship rules.

order: Content accuracy, specificity, redundancy, task fit, paragraph and sentence rhythm as editorial observations
conditional_rankings.caveat: No measured detector AUROC transfers to visual cue lists or humanization efficacy.

linguistic.scope: Primary-source review of arXiv 2606.04177v1 and 2505.01800v1, including appendices; no canonical skill edits

source_2606.title: A Systematic Analysis of Linguistic Features in AI-Generated Text Detection Across Domains and Models
source_2606.license: CC BY-SA 4.0, per arXiv HTML header
source_2606.status: empirical English-language classification study, not a human-reviewer validation of prose judgments
source_2606.population: MAGE English passages: ten source domains; 27 generation models in seven families; continuation prompts only. Train 93,318 human and 194,839 AI; validation 28,799 human and 24,151 AI; test 28,741 human and 24,226 AI. Separate GPT-4 test: CNN/DailyMail, DialogSum, IMDb, PubMed. CMV prompt pilot also used direct-response prompts.
source_2606.inventory_caveat: The paper calls Appendix A.3 a full list, but gives grouped descriptions for several categories, not 284 unique machine-readable feature names. Counts below are from Table 5 and sum to 284. Do not invent missing variable names or map unnamed members to specific lexicons/UD labels without the ELFEN extraction schema.

named_features: count of words longer than five characters
raw sequence length including spaces and special characters
feature_groups.direction: No stable human-vs-AI direction established at individual-feature level; raw length can track prompt/source domain. Appendix E.1 notes sequence length, token, syllable and lemma counts differ among human domains.

named_features: type-token ratio (number of distinct tokens divided by token count)
global token hapax legomena (tokens in a passage appearing only once in the full corpus, per A.3.4)
lexical density (adjective+noun+verb+adverb tokens divided by token count)
feature_groups.definition_ref: Appendix A.3.4; Appendix C.4.3; Appendix D.2
feature_groups.direction: Paper's distribution prose claims greater human values for all three, but also reports human TTR near 0.6 and AI TTR near 0.8; Appendix D.2 explicitly says human TTR lower and AI TTR/lexical density higher. Human raw global-hapax count is reported higher, with passage-length dependence. Do not impose a universal sign.

named_features: high-intensity token counts by Plutchik emotion
low-intensity token counts by Plutchik emotion
feature_groups.direction: Illustrative Yelp pairs show higher human anger/disgust intensity and low-valence counts; AI samples have higher valence. This is a selected domain-model illustration, not a general direction. Group ablation changes sign by domain.

named_features: high/low concreteness token counts and average rating
high/low age-of-acquisition token counts and average rating
high/low prevalence token counts and average rating
high/low socialness token counts and average rating
high/low iconicity token counts and average rating
high/low sensorimotor-association token counts and average rating
feature_groups.direction: No individual-direction claim. Group's value reverses across domains; removing it helps unseen WritingPrompts/ROCStories but harms unseen CMV/XSum/SciGen in the reported ablations.
No stable human-vs-AI direction. Ablation effect small or adverse in aggregate and domain dependent.

named_features: all nonuniform Universal Dependencies morphological features in the data; individual features are not enumerated
feature_groups.direction: Group helps some seen settings, hurts some unseen domains, notably DialogSum.

named_features: token frequency for each Universal Dependencies POS tag; tags not enumerated in paper
POS variability (number of distinct POS tags divided by token count)
feature_groups.direction: No stable individual direction; POS group especially useful for short SQuAD responses in one in-domain ablation.

named_features: count for each Universal Dependencies dependency-relation type; labels not enumerated
feature_groups.direction: No stable individual direction; group depends on text and model domain.

named_features: mean synset count overall and separately for nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs
high-synset-count token count overall and separately for nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs
low-synset-count token count overall and separately for nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs
feature_groups.direction: No stable individual direction; removing semantic group hurts unseen DialogSum in Appendix C.2.

named_features: entity count for each entity type; type names not enumerated
feature_groups.direction: No stable individual direction. Group often marginal; source/topic naturally affects entity counts.
No stable human-vs-AI sign. Second most influential group on mixed in-domain TB4 but often hurts unseen text-domain performance (Appendix C.1).

features_explicitly_excluded: additional theoretically equivalent surface, readability, and lexical-richness metrics
source_2606.feature_preprocessing: Most counts are divided by token count; raw type, sentence, character, lemma, and syllable counts are exceptions. Uniform features are removed; missing/infinite values imputed by feature type; z-score scaling is fit on train data. Linear balanced SVM, C=1.0, seed 42. §3.2 and Appendix A.2.

task_conditional_ranks.evidence: Table 5 full macro F1 .827; remove lexical richness .696 (about -13.1 percentage points); remove information .809 (about -1.8); all other removals at most about -0.6 points by printed rounded values. Lexical-only cumulative experiment retains .776, about -5.0 points versus all features. This ranks feature groups for this classifier, not individual features.

task_conditional_ranks.setting: TB7 four new domains plus GPT-4
task_conditional_ranks.evidence: Table 5 full macro F1 .808; remove lexical richness .531 (about -27.7 points); most other removals increase F1, particularly morphology .846 and psycholinguistics .834. Appendix C.4 says lexical-only exceeded full model by 14.29 points, yet domain F1 spans CNN .9682 to DialogSum .5024 (Table 11).

task_conditional_ranks.setting: TB2 seen model family, mixed domains
task_conditional_ranks.evidence: Table 16: removing lexical richness improves OpenAI +.003, LLaMA +.022, GLM +.025, but harms FLAN-T5 -.095, OPT -.032, BigScience -.057, Eleuther -.024. Apparent lexical ranking reverses for several families.
Table 16: removing lexical richness harms all seven families, from Eleuther -.029 to LLaMA -.174. Information group also harms each family when removed (roughly -.015 to -.026).
Table 16: removing lexical richness harms nine of ten domains, worst ELI5 -.118; SQuAD improves +.002. For SQuAD, removing surface -.034, emotion -.019, POS -.014. Other groups vary.

Table 16: removing lexical richness harms every domain, from SQuAD -.003 to XSum -.274. Removing psycholinguistic improves WritingPrompts +.037 and lowers CMV -.011, XSum -.011; information removal lowers most domains but improves ROCStories +.036. Thus category rankings are setting-specific.

task_conditional_ranks.setting: TB8 unseen text AND model families, 70 pairs
task_conditional_ranks.evidence: Table 12 mean macro F1 .587, range .345-.889. Full ablation performed only for 16 selected pairs (Appendix C.3). Lexical-only versus full for 70 pairs (Appendix C.4): ROCStories +10.1 to +15.3 points; WritingPrompts mostly improves but OPT -20.0, LLaMA -16.6; SciGen, SQuAD and HellaSwag mostly worsen. OpenAI mean +.0528. No universal lexical-only rule.

direction_and_internal_consistency: Appendix C.4.3 says human values exceed AI on all three lexical metrics, yet its TTR centers (human ~0.6, AI ~0.8) imply the opposite. Appendix D.2 explicitly supports lower human TTR and higher AI TTR and lexical density; human raw hapax count is higher with longer passages. Treat the all-three-human-higher assertion as internally inconsistent.

Appendix A.3.4 defines hapax as corpus-global singleton tokens per passage; Appendix C.4.3 and D.2 sometimes describe words appearing once in a text. These are different measures, so do not collapse them.
Ablation measures a group's marginal effect in a trained multifeature classifier; it does not assign an authorship direction, causal mechanism, or calibrated confidence to a single passage.
Text and model domain reversals make a categorical checklist or universal weights unsupported.
false_positives_and_limits: Paper reports macro F1/AUROC and sometimes per-class recall, but no calibrated false-positive rate or human false-positive analysis in its main comparison. Cannot translate F1 to a probability that a single passage was machine-written.
TB8 cross-generalization F1 as low as .345; DialogSum GPT-4 F1 .5024, so transfer can approach poor performance. Tables 11–12.
Prompts mostly held to continuation; pilot changing prompt also changed model composition. Appendix B.2's model-family alignment claim is suggestive rather than isolated causal proof.
Benchmark generations do not cover newest models as of study; no direct evidence for edited/hybrid prose or adversarial rewriting; language is English. §5 Limitations.
Most counts can reflect passage length, prompt, topic, register, quotations, and document conventions; authors warn about domain/model and dataset confounds in §2 and §5.
Tool extraction and lexicons require language-specific validation; do not transfer these English distributions to Russian or another language.
qualitative_skill_implications: Inspect lexical repetition, generic word reuse, specific word choice and content-word density as review prompts, then verify against genre, passage length, topic and author voice; do not demand maximized TTR or novelty.

Use meaning-first checks for unsupported claims, generic filler, redundant transitions, and unnatural sentiment in the actual rhetorical context, without presenting them as diagnostic features proven here.
Describe evidence as observed text features with excerpts and uncertainty, never authorship verdict or numeric risk without a calibrated detector.
Preserve useful repetitions, terminology, natural formality, and intentional reader guidance during revision. Humanization should improve substance and voice, not optimize a detector score.
needs_tools_and_calibration: Exact TTR, global hapax, lexical density, POS, UD morphology/dependencies, NER, sentiment, psycholinguistic ratings, synset metrics, entropy, compressibility and readability require defined tokenizer/lexicon/parser plus validation for the target language/genre.

A classifier-style ranking or authorship probability requires matched human and model baselines, evaluation across new generators and prompts, predeclared thresholds, and a reported human false-positive rate.
A corpus-global hapax metric is impossible from a lone passage without its reference corpus; passage-local hapax is a different measure.

source_2505.title: Distinguishing AI-Generated and Human-Written Text Through Psycholinguistic Analysis
source_2505.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, per arXiv HTML header
source_2505.status: theoretical mapping of prior StyloAI stylometric features to psycholinguistic interpretations; no new classifier, benchmark, ablation, sample count, error analysis, or feature ranking is reported in this paper
source_2505.population: No new evaluated population reported. Examples are said to be from a previous StyloAI dataset, with isolated passages and no representativeness data in this paper.
source_2505.count_discrepancy: Text claims 31 features and Table 1 says 18 mapped; Appendix Table 2 lists 29 distinct named rows (6 lexical, 11 syntactic, 4 sentiment, 2 readability, 4 named-entity category, 2 uniqueness), while Table 1 lists 19 distinct names. Verified in HTML and PDF. Do not supply two invented names to reach 31.
inventory_appendix_table_2: distinct words divided by total words
sentences with more than one clause
number of nouns for intangible concepts
number of less frequent verbs; threshold unspecified
number of adjectives treated as complex; examples use -ive/-ous suffixes, operational rule unspecified
number of words in an emotion lexicon
estimated education years needed for first reading
number of first-person pronouns; despite category label this is not NER
reader-address instances; despite category label this is not NER
count of novel bigram/trigram combinations; novelty baseline unspecified
range of sentence structures; operational definition unspecified
theoretical_directions: §3.1 suggests humans often use more context-specific vocabulary, varied syntax, situated sentiment, and grounded entities; AI may be more repetitive, generic, or tonally flat. These are hypotheses/interpretations, not measured direction estimates in this paper.
§2 also admits human cognitive load can cause simplification, errors, repeated words, abrupt shifts, and weak transitions, so those are possible human traits too.
The paper's claim that AI cannot self-monitor, revise deliberately, or adapt rhetorically is a theoretical stance; these internal cognitive properties cannot be inferred from text alone.
High word count, long words, first-person pronouns, emotion words and unusual phrasing are not independently verified indicators of human authorship here.
source_2505.ranking_evidence: None in this paper. No weights, ablation, F1, effect sizes, false-positive rates, or model/genre comparisons for the 29 listed features. Do not rank them by Table 1 grouping or cited cognitive theory.
limitations_and_false_positives: No false-positive evaluation, thus no basis for individual authorship judgments or academic-integrity sanctions.
Table 2's 29/31 and Table 1's 19/18 discrepancies undermine treating the inventory as a validated, complete 31-feature set.
Examples are selected and drawn from prior work; no sampling method or control for genre, topic, length or learner style is supplied here.
Several descriptions are nonoperational (complex verbs/adjectives, novel n-grams, syntax variety); lexical metrics depend on length and tokenization.
Feature category mislabels first-person reference and direct address as named entities.
English examples and formulas cannot be presumed validated for Russian or other languages; no multilingual evaluation here.
Claims about emotional authenticity, lived experience, metacognition and cognitive load should not be used as text-based proofs of author identity.
qualitative_skill_implications: As a theory-informed editing lens, consider whether vocabulary, sentence shape, emotional tone, entity use and reader address fit the author's purpose and subject.
Treat apparent repetition, complexity, pronouns, punctuation, or sentiment as questions for contextual review, never deterministic AI flags.
For revision, explain concrete effects on clarity, specificity and voice; do not add personal anecdotes, mistakes, emotions or entities to imitate humans.
needs_tools_and_calibration: Actual feature extraction needs operational definitions, suitable language resources, human reference samples, genre/length matching, and prospective false-positive testing.
The psycholinguistic mapping itself needs controlled empirical testing before it can justify ranking or diagnosis.

linguistic.copyright_note: Only short technical feature names and original paraphrased descriptions/findings are recorded; no source tables, prose passages, scripts or figure assets are copied. The second source is noncommercial share-alike licensed; a derivative reproduction would need separate license review. This research-note JSON records factual observations and attribution, not adapted source prose.
linguistic.overall_recommendation: For an ai-detector skill, use feature families as context-dependent prompts and explicitly avoid numerical or categorical authorship claims without calibrated evidence. For a humanizer skill, revise one meaningful prose issue at a time to support the author's purpose and preserve factual content, rather than optimizing a surface-feature score. Explicitly distinguish empirically tested English category ablations (2606) from theoretical cognitive interpretations (2505).

discourse.note_type: Original factual research synthesis; no source prose, tables, scripts or examples copied for adaptation

sources.title: Relational Over-Regularization: Graph-Based AI-Generated Text Detection via Sentence Transition Deviation
sources.scope: arXiv v1 preprint, 27 August 2026. Four benchmark pools (HC3 professional/ChatGPT; M4 multi-domain/multi-generator; MULTITuDE multilingual/eight generators; AIGTBench social-media/twelve generators). ROR validation: each pool 1000 human and 1000 AI documents. Held-out: 500 continuations each from Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against a shared set of 500 human documents. Continuation prompt supplies first 30 document tokens; temperature 1.0; no per-language feature results. Standard supervised evaluation 70/15/15 split and ten runs (§4, Appendix A/E).

definitions.computation: Variance, per document, of cosine similarities between consecutive frozen RoBERTa CLS sentence embeddings; compare distributions of per-document values with Mann-Whitney U and rank-biserial r (§3.1, Table 1).
definitions.direction: Higher AI in the four pooled benchmarks, but GPT-5 held-out is lower than human (Appendix C Table 9).

definitions.computation: Cosine similarity of sentence pair minus that document's mean cosine similarity over all unordered sentence pairs; positive = unusually similar pair, negative = unusually dissimilar pair (§3.2 Eq.4).
definitions.direction: Some AI output has local similarity bursts; GPT-5 has smaller absolute deviations. This is a graph feature, not a universal prose target.

definitions.computation: Cosine similarity of any graph-linked pair (§3.2 Eq.3).
Absolute sentence-index gap divided by sentence count minus one (§3.2 Eq.3).
definitions.direction: No standalone group direction; its ablation causes largest of four edge-component accuracy losses (0.25 pp; Appendix B.3).

definitions.computation: Binary edge feature for neighboring sentences; all neighbors linked; additional long-range edges if cosine similarity exceeds theta=0.6 (§3.2).

Hedge-word ratio, modal-verb ratio, first-person pronoun ratio, question and exclamation marks, token count, type-token ratio, comma density, discourse-marker presence, long-word ratio (§3.2 Node Features).
definitions.direction: Listed as model inputs, with no separate feature directions or ablations in this paper.

definitions.computation: Authors' proposed explanation of variance pattern; each mechanism lacks a separate annotation count or isolated test (§1, §3.1, §5.1).
definitions.direction: Proposed for some AI generators; formulaic human news also exhibits recurring patterns (Appendix D.1).

detector_results: Standard balanced Setting 1: CSFG accuracy/FPR/FNR = 97.14/1.57/4.15%; CoCo graph baseline 86.00/23.00/5.00%; SeqXGPT 93.02/12.43/1.53% (§5.2 Table 2). These are classifier outcomes, not prevalence estimates of stylistic traits.

Source-attribution auxiliary-loss lambda 0 to 1: accuracy 96.25→97.22%; FPR 2.27→1.48%; FNR 5.23→4.08%. The prose says both error rates decline consistently, but the intermediate table values are not strictly monotone (Appendix B.1 Table 5).
Semantic-edge theta 0.3–0.7: accuracy 97.14–97.23%, FPR 1.45–1.58%, FNR 4.01–4.16%; validation AUROC selects 0.6 (Appendix B.2 Table 6).

Edge ablation full accuracy/FPR/FNR 97.14/1.57/4.15%; omit cosine 96.92/1.59/4.57; omit distance 96.89/1.54/4.67; omit adjacency flag 96.94/1.69/4.42; omit delta 96.97/1.65/4.40 (Appendix B.3 Table 7). Effects are small, with no isolated confidence test.
perturbation_and_boundary_results: Claude-generated AI after Claude paraphrase/humanization/back-translation: CSFG accuracy 90.59/87.43/90.96%, FPR on perturbed human documents 88.24/84.31/49.80%, FNR 1.22/5.10/4.79% (§5.4 Table 4). LLM rewriting of human controls drives FPR; no human rewrite or separate-family rewriter control.

Gemini equivalent accuracy/FPR/FNR: paraphrase 85.98/92.16/5.91%, humanization 76.43/82.35/17.48%, back-translation 91.53/37.25/5.49%. GPT-5: 77.86/36.73/20.63%, 47.93/20.00/55.35%, 86.31/22.58/12.84%. GPT-5 humanization is a severe exception (Appendix D.2 Table 14).

Under 500 characters, N=125 per generator, accuracy/FPR/FNR Claude 56.00/63.86/4.76%; Gemini 51.20/71.08/4.76%; GPT-5 74.40/18.07/40.48%. Too few pairs destabilize the statistic (Appendix D.1 Table 12).
Professionally edited XSum human news, N=100, reported FPR 25% versus 1.57% standard. Its recurring conventional restatements overlap the proposed signal (Appendix D.1 Table 13).
limits_and_anomalies: Pooled-benchmark variance is on a 10^-6 scale, held-out Appendix C variance on a 10^-3 scale; no explanation given for direct numerical comparability.
Appendix D Tables 10–11 label 0.xx accuracy/error entries as percentages; Table 14 supplies corresponding xx% values. Use Table 14.
Human-only XSum Table 13 reports FPR 25%, accuracy 85%, and FNR 6%; those three values cannot all be interpreted as defined in §4. Do not reuse accuracy/FNR.
The delta ablation's FPR shift is 0.08 pp with no significance test; its claimed false-positive calibration role is a tentative interpretation.

Mechanism attribution to next-token training and RLHF was proposed, not experimentally manipulated. Potential confounds include genre, length, prompt, generator, embedding representation, creative/high-temperature writing. Semantic edge computation quadratic (§6).
sources.safe_transfer: For longer prose, inspect whether adjacent sentences or paragraphs redundantly restate the same idea; edit only when purpose and meaning allow. Treat structural similarity as a contextual question, never an authorship verdict or a target score. Preserve legitimate repetitive structure in short, academic, news and instructional work.
sources.unsafe_transfer: Do not prescribe arbitrary topic drift, jagged similarity, random sentence-length changes or damaged coherence to appear human. Do not assert every generator has inflated variance. Do not infer universal detector accuracy from this benchmark or treat a single short sample as proof of AI authorship.

sources.title: Linguistic comparison of AI- and human-written responses to online mental health queries
sources.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Noncommercial redistribution with attribution permitted; adapted material is not licensed. Notes below independently paraphrase factual observations. Do not adapt source prose, tables, examples or code.
sources.scope: English Reddit mental-health peer-support genre: 24,114 posts and 138,758 peer replies from 55 subreddits, 2018-01-01 to 2024-03-31. One zero-shot GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1, Mistral-7B reply generated for each post using default parameters and no added system/role/style/safety prompt. GPT is main comparison; Llama and Mistral robustness checks. Paired tests compare each model reply to the mean of all human replies to that post, giving one matched pair per post. Qualitative 50 posts; separate random 100 AI responses rated by one psychologist (§Methods, Tables 1-5).

measurement_methods.LIWC: Normalized occurrences in eight psycholinguistic categories; paired t and KS tests with Bonferroni correction; GPT Cohen d. Many tiny differences are significant at large N, so attend to effect size (§Results Table 1; §Methods).
measurement_methods.verbosity: Words per reply and mean words per sentence.
measurement_methods.Coleman_Liau: CLI = 0.0588L - 0.296S - 15.8, where L is letters per 100 words and S is sentences per 100 words. Higher grade means more demanding surface form, not better comprehension.
measurement_methods.complexity: Mean word length per sentence as defined by authors; a narrow proxy, not semantic sophistication.
measurement_methods.categorical_dynamic_index: 30 + articles + prepositions - personal pronouns - impersonal pronouns - auxiliary verbs - conjunctions - adverbs - negations, using LIWC frequencies; higher = more categorical/analytical style.
measurement_methods.formality_empathy_politeness: Separate classifier scores 0-1, not user-rated outcomes. Sanity check on 185 AI replies gives 98.9%, 98.4%, 98.4% label agreement with human judgment. Empathy classifier trained on reactions to news.
measurement_methods.query_semantic_similarity: Cosine similarity of query and response from 300-dimensional Google News word embeddings.
measurement_methods.style_accommodation: Cosine similarity of normalized function-word LIWC vectors for query and reply.
measurement_methods.cross_reply_diversity: Each reply's cosine distance to centroid of its own group's word-embedding vectors; population-level measure, not a single-answer creativity test.
measurement_methods.emotional_informational_support: Binary support SVMs trained/validated in prior peer-support work, validation accuracy 0.71 and 0.77 respectively; outputs are linguistic proxies (§Methods).

sources.lexicosemantic_inventory_format: Each row = [feature, OC human mean, GPT mean, GPT Cohen d, Llama mean, Mistral mean], from Results Tables 2 and 5. Tables mark most pairwise tests p<.001; measurement meaning in Methods.
sources.liwc_inventory_format: Each row = [feature, OC human mean, GPT mean, GPT relative percent, GPT Cohen d, Llama mean, Mistral mean], from Results Tables 1 and 4. Means rounded; zero/equal at shown precision does not imply exact zero/equality.
sources.qualitative_observations: In 50 sampled threads, GPT replies often began by acknowledging difficulty then gave ordered, reusable general advice, commonly in bullets; human peers often focused on one suggestion, sought clarification or follow-up, and related actual experiences. GPT more often supplied a neutral account of treatment tradeoffs while peers explained their own positions. GPT sometimes answered experience-seeking with generic information or referral. Authors observed one reply that inserted a nonexistent situation detail. These are themes, with no prevalence counts (§Robustness qualitative findings).
sources.clinical_check: One psychologist rated random N=100 AI replies on 1-5 scales. Factual accuracy mean 5.00 (SD 0; 100% at least 4); potential harmfulness mean 1.14 (SD .35; 0% at least 4); emotional attunement mean 1.82 (SD .99; 0% at least 4); contextual responsiveness mean 2.64 (SD .67; 0% at least 4). No direct unsafe advice in this sample; possible indirect concerns from vague reassurance, low acknowledgment of distress, and absent risk-sensitive language. This sample and qualitative hallucination example differ (§Robustness Table 3).
sources.generator_exceptions: Sadness higher than OC for GPT, lower for Llama/Mistral. Auxiliary verbs higher for GPT/Mistral, lower for Llama. Impersonal pronouns higher for GPT, lower for Llama, approximately equal for Mistral. Present focus higher for GPT/Mistral, lower for Llama; future focus lower for GPT/Llama, slightly higher for Mistral. Most striking: formality/empathy/politeness classifier scores 0.03-0.04 for Llama/Mistral versus 0.67-0.71 for OC and 0.79-0.87 for GPT, contradicting broad prose about AI being higher on these (§Results Tables 4-5).
limitations_and_quality_flags: Self-selected English Reddit mental-health community participants; single-response exchanges; no multi-turn tests. Human replies often served different purposes from one-shot AI answers. Do not universalize to other genres, languages, or models (§Discussion).
Large word-count gap (GPT 160 vs OC 77; Llama 471; Mistral 332). Some normalized measures, but no explicit length matching/control (§Methods; §Discussion).

Automated empathy/support scores are proxies, not perceived help or emotional effect. Support SVM validation only .71/.77. Clinical sample small with one rater; full source corpus unavailable for privacy (§Methods; Data availability).
Paper says higher 'readability' but CLI 11.19 versus 6.58 actually means higher grade burden. Prose says OC CLI 6.90 while tables give 6.58; use tabulated value (§Results Table 2).

GPT CDI percentage is 40.04% in Table 2 but 60% in prose. Style-accommodation d .21 in table but .76 in prose. Diversity d -.89 in table but -1.21 in prose. Sexual LIWC difference -88.34% in Table 1 but -30% in prose. Prefer tables and avoid disputed statistics.

Table 4 significance stars appear on some rounded-equal rows or rows Table 1 labels nonsignificant. Table 5 Llama/Mistral classifier scores are striking and unexplained; do not extend GPT proxy claims to all AI.
Table 3's generic footnote says higher score means stronger safety, while its potential-harmfulness dimension is reverse-valued. Interpret that column by its label and text.

Only use as context questions, never quotas or authorship evidence.

sources.unsafe_transfer: Never fabricate first-person memories, relationships, chronology, medical facts or a human identity. Do not add profanity, slang, misplaced questions, an ungrounded treatment stance, or reduce safety language to imitate peers. Do not claim classifier-rated empathy proves emotional benefit or that the observed genre pattern establishes authorship.

Table 16: removing lexical richness harms nine of ten domains, worst ELI5 -.118; SQuAD improves +.002. For SQuAD, removing surface -.034, emotion -.019, POS -.014. Other groups vary.

Table 16: removing lexical richness harms every domain, from SQuAD -.003 to XSum -.274. Removing psycholinguistic improves WritingPrompts +.037 and lowers CMV -.011, XSum -.011; information removal lowers most domains but improves ROCStories +.036. Thus category rankings are setting-specific.
